case_name: Mixed-direction 10% bucket — aggregate passes despite one large increase
computation: Zero bucket: LE=1500+800+450=2750, CD=1500+800+450=2750, Δ=0 → no violation. 10% bucket: LE_agg=120+300+500=920, 10% threshold=920×1.10=1012. CD_agg=100+480+520=1100. NOTE THE DEFECT THIS SUITE CATCHES: sum of individual increases inside 10% bucket = (100-120=-20)+(480-300=+180)+(520-500=+20) = +180; if you wrongly test 'sum of increases ≤ 10% of LE_agg' you get 180 ≤ 92 → false → spurious violation. Correct test is aggregate-vs-aggregate: CD_agg (1100) vs LE_agg (920); permitted max = 1012; 1100 > 1012 → VIOLATION. The mixed directions (recording fee decreased 20, title increased 180) are exactly why aggregate comparison is required. 10% excess = 1100 − 1012 = 88. No-limit bucket: not tested. Total cure = 88.

violations.ten_pct_aggregate: VIOLATION — aggregate CD 1100 exceeds permitted 1012 by 88
violations.clause_basis: 12 CFR §1026.19(e)(3)(ii) — aggregate of charges for third-party services and recording fees cannot exceed aggregate disclosed by more than 10%; cure per §1026.19(f)(2)(v) refunding excess within 60 days of consummation

weakest_point: Assigned 'Title search' and 'Settlement agent' to 10% bucket on the fact premise that borrower shopped and selected from lender's written list; if no valid written list existed, these would drop to zero_tolerance and cure would be much larger.

computation: Zero bucket: LE=700+250=950, CD=700+250=950, Δ=0 → no violation. 10% bucket: LE_agg=200+350+180+120=850, threshold=850×1.10=935. CD_agg=150+420+220+90=880. Sum-of-increases test (WRONG) would compute: recording −50, title +70, survey +40, pest −30 → net +30; 30 ≤ 85 → would pass anyway here, but the correct aggregate test is CD_agg vs LE_agg: 880 ≤ 935 → PASS. Mixed directions present (recording ↓50, pest ↓30, title ↑70, survey ↑40) so aggregate comparison is mandatory. No 10% violation. No-limit not tested. Total cure = 0.

case_name: Clean pass — all buckets within tolerance
computation: Zero bucket: LE=100+1400+50=1550, CD=100+1400+50=1550, Δ=0 → no violation. 10% bucket: LE_agg=90+600+250=940, threshold=940×1.10=1034. CD_agg=95+650+270=1015. 1015 ≤ 1034 → PASS (note: even though settlement fee alone rose 50/600≈8.3% and title search rose 20/250=8%, the aggregate test is what governs). No-limit not tested. Total cure = 0.
weakest_point: Assumed all 10%-bucket providers were on lender's written list; documentation in file should confirm.

case_name: 10% bucket violation with all increases same direction (baseline case)
computation: Zero bucket: LE=CD=1000 → no violation. 10% bucket: LE_agg=80+400+500+150=1130, threshold=1130×1.10=1243. CD_agg=88+470+560+180=1298. 1298 > 1243 → VIOLATION. 10% excess = 1298 − 1243 = 55. Here all items increased, so sum-of-increases (=8+70+60+30=168) and aggregate test agree there is a violation, but the cure amount differs: sum-of-increases would suggest curing 168, but correct cure is the aggregate excess = 55 (the maximum refund needed to bring CD_agg down to 1243). This demonstrates that even when directional signs agree, the aggregate excess — not sum of increases — is the cure. No-limit not tested. Total cure = 55.

violations.ten_pct_aggregate: VIOLATION — CD aggregate 1298 exceeds permitted 1243 by 55
violations.clause_basis: 12 CFR §1026.19(e)(3)(ii) — aggregate cannot exceed disclosed aggregate by more than 10%; cure = CD_agg − 1.10×LE_agg per §1026.19(f)(2)(v)

weakest_point: Cure amount of 55 is the aggregate excess, which is less than the simple sum of line-item increases (168) because the 10% threshold already permits some increase; implementations that cure 'sum of increases' over-refund.
